title: IonQ Demonstrates 1 kHz Memory-Enhanced Quantum Interconnect Connecting Trapped Ions and Diamond Color Centers - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IonQ demonstrated a heralded photonic interconnect between a trapped 138Ba+ ion and a diamond SiV− quantum memory at 1.032 kHz with 87.9% fidelity, claimed as the fastest heralded inter-node entanglement rate to date and 4x the prior trapped-ion record. A single-photon reflection protocol makes success scale linearly rather than quadratically with photon efficiency, and a foundry-compatible diamond thin-film process with Element Six and AWS targets scalable manufacturing. (The article opens with an image caption about thin-film production steps.)

insights.claim: IonQ demonstrated heralded entanglement between a trapped 138Ba+ ion and a diamond silicon-vacancy memory at 1.032 kHz (1,032 Bell pairs per second) with 87.9% state fidelity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Kilohertz networking is a key enabler for modular, scale-out trapped-ion machines.

insights.claim: IonQ claims this is the fastest heralded entanglement rate between separate quantum nodes to date, four times the previous trapped-ion benchmark.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Strengthens IonQ's technical lead narrative in distributed quantum computing.
insights.quote: the fastest heralded entanglement rate demonstrated between separate quantum nodes to date, exceeding the previous trapped-ion benchmark by a factor of four

insights.claim: The ~969 µs mean time to success matches the roughly 1 ms cycle time of planned fault-tolerant trapped-ion processors, meaning networking no longer has to be the bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Interconnect speed parity with compute cycles makes multi-QPU fault tolerance architecturally viable.

insights.claim: The infidelity budget breaks down as 4.3% from the ion node, 3.9% from the diamond memory, 2.9% from frequency conversion and 1.9% from detection/photon loss.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: No single dominant error source; fidelity gains require improvements across several subsystems.

insights.claim: Conventional two-photon heralding has success probability scaling quadratically (p²) with per-attempt photon delivery efficiency because two photons must be detected simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains why photonic interconnect rates have historically been poor.

insights.claim: IonQ replaces two-photon interference with a single-photon reflection off a cavity-coupled SiV− memory, so success scales linearly (p) with collection efficiency.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Linear rather than quadratic scaling is a structural advantage that compounds as efficiencies improve.

insights.claim: The heterogeneous design combines the optical coherence of atomic qubits with the photon-coupling efficiency of cavity-coupled solid-state memories to address the photon-loss bottleneck in distributed quantum networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Heterogeneous modality integration may become a differentiator versus single-modality rivals.

insights.claim: The link uses polarization-insensitive frequency conversion from 493.5 nm to 737.45 nm in a Sagnac PPLN crystal, and the diamond memory operates in a 20 mK dilution refrigerator.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The memory layer still requires dilution refrigeration, adding cost and complexity to the stack.

insights.claim: With Element Six and AWS, IonQ developed a foundry-compatible diamond thin-film pipeline with near-unity membrane transfer yield, cooperativities of about 92-100 and sub-1 dB fiber packaging loss.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Moving diamond memories from academic cleanrooms to foundry processes is necessary for volume networking hardware.

insights.claim: The milestone advances IonQ's work under DARPA's HARQ program, which targets QPU-agnostic networking fabrics linking trapped ions, neutral atoms and transduced superconducting circuits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions IonQ as a potential networking supplier even to rival qubit modalities.

insights.claim: The interconnect hardware builds on IonQ's acquisitions of Lightsynq Technologies and Oxford Ionics and deployments to University of Maryland's QLab and SDT in South Korea.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows IonQ's M&A roll-up is producing integrated technical results.
